newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan braces for Typhoon Sally, issues warnings.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan braces for Typhoon Sally, issues warnings.

text.p: Taiwan issued a land warning for mid-range Typhoon Sally on Saturday, with the government urging people to be prepared after Typhoon Herb in August caused the most serious damage in three decades.
The Central Weather Bureau's land warning was issued at 3.00 p.m. (0700 GMT). A sea warning was posted Saturday morning.

Sally, located 590 km (369 miles) southeast of southern Taiwan on Saturday afternoon, was moving west-northwest at 28 kmh (17.5 mph) toward the island with maximum sustained winds of 137 kmh (85.5 mph) and gusts of up to 173 kmh (108 mph).
Sally was expected to bring torrential rains to southern and southeastern Taiwan, and may affect northern Taiwan on Sunday, the bureau said.
The cabinet's Council of Agriculture, in a statement on Saturday, urged people to be prepared.
Sally would be the fourth typhoon to hit Taiwan in 1996 after Gloria killed three people and caused damage estimated at T$580 million (US$21 million).
Typhoon Herb claimed 45 lives and caused an estimated T$19.76 billion (US$719 million) in agricultural losses and T$2.58 billion (US$94 million) in infrastructure and road damage.
Lisa, the third typhoon, caused little damage. ($1 = T$27.5)
